summary: Streaming token metering spike during regional failover — duplicate counts observed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected spike in billed streaming tokens on 2026-02-28 during a planned network failover. Usage dashboard shows a ~2x increase in token consumption for streaming sessions that overlapped the failover window. Customer states application traffic and request patterns did not change. They are requesting a breakdown and credit for duplicated token charges if billing is incorrect.

Impact:
NimbusChat reports an unexpected bill delta of ~120M streaming tokens for the billing day, affecting their month-to-date spend and causing internal budget alerts. Business impact: finance escalation and potential delay to customer rollout.

Environment:
Production (prod-us-east-1), dedicated capacity ran with graceful region failover to us-west for ~14 minutes. Streaming endpoints: /v1/streams/generate. Model: rwd-chat-3.2 pinned.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer established long-lived streaming sessions against prod-us-east endpoint.
2) At 03:14 UTC on 2026-02-28 the control-plane initiated a regional failover to us-west due to transient networking in us-east.
3) Several stream connections were re-established and resumed output; billing dashboard shows both pre-failover and post-failover token increments for the same session IDs.

Notes: customer logs include reconnect timestamps that align with the failover window.
expected_behavior: During failover, streaming requests should be routed to fallback without double-counting tokens. Metering should dedupe the same logical session/offsets so customers are not billed twice for in-flight tokens.
actual_behavior: Metering recorded token consumption on both the original and the fallback path for overlapping time ranges. The effect was near-duplicate counts for streaming frames that were retried or resumed after connection handoff.
raw_logs:
2026-02-28T03:13:58Z prod-us-east ingress req_id=abc123 stream_id=s-74 token_count=120
2026-02-28T03:14:02Z control-plane failover start
2026-02-28T03:14:05Z prod-us-west ingress req_id=abc123 stream_id=s-74 token_count=118
2026-02-28T03:14:10Z prod-us-west ingress req_id=abc123 stream_id=s-74 token_count=6
(aggregator shows both entries attributed to same customer account)
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: duplicate counting because request-id was propagated but metering aggregator did not dedupe during transient multi-path traffic.
- Confirmed with logs: same request_id (customer-provided X-Request-ID) was seen on both regions. Metering pipeline uses a regional shard key which caused both shards to record counts independently during the handoff window.
- Billing pipeline stores per-shard increments and a final reconciliation job runs daily; however, reconciliation did not mark these as duplicates because session offset metadata was missing for streaming frames.
- Reproduce locally with simulated failover: created an integration test that opens a stream, simulates re-attach on fallback, and observed duplicate meter increments in the test aggregator.
- Temporary mitigation: disabled per-shard immediate flush for streaming meter increments during failover window and enabled a short dedupe grace window (PR linked).
comments: Ava Patel (Support): Received initial report from NimbusChat billing team at 2026-02-28T10:50Z. Requesting urgent triage and probable credit.
Miguel Rivera (SRE): I'm investigating metering shards and routing. Early sign points to lack of dedupe across regions when the same request_id appears. Allocated time to confirm and prototype fix.
Claire Zhang (Billing): Can we quantify token delta per account? Need explicit numbers to propose credit. I'll compile raw increments and estimated duplicates.

Miguel Rivera (SRE): Deployed hotfix to add request-id dedupe in aggregator and a reconciliation rule to retroactively collapse obvious duplicates. Patch rolled out to prod at 2026-03-01T02:20Z. Monitoring for 24h.
resolution:
Workaround and fix applied: added request-id based dedupe in the regional aggregator and a reconciliation job to collapse duplicate streaming increments detected in the 2026-02-28 failover window. Computed duplicate token count for NimbusChat: 118,742,540 tokens. Billing has applied a one-time credit for the duplicated tokens on 2026-03-02.

Follow-ups: scheduled postmortem and runbook updates to include a dedupe-grace window for future failovers; action item recorded for platform to propagate streaming offset metadata to billing pipeline (tracked in GH PR and Confluence). Customer notified and finance confirmation received.

Status: Resolved for customer billing; ticket kept open until postmortem published (target 2026-03-10).
notes_for_escalation: Recommend review of per-region shard boundaries for metering and adding an idempotency header requirement in streaming SDKs. Consider an opt-in 'strict-metering' mode for enterprise tenants that preserves offsets.
